title: Make Array Strictly Increasing
summary: Given two integer arrays arr1 and arr2, determine the least number of operations required to make arr1 strictly increasing.
statement: Given two integer arrays arr1 and arr2, determine the least number of operations required to make arr1 strictly increasing. An operation involves selecting an index from arr1 and assigning it a value from arr2. If it's impossible to make arr1 strictly increasing, return -1.
constraints: Each arr1 position may be replaced by any arr2 value.
Return -1 when strict increase is impossible.
hints: A state maps the last chosen value to the fewest replacements so far.
At each position, keep arr1 value if it exceeds the previous state value.
Also binary-search the smallest arr2 value strictly larger than the previous value and charge one.
Keeping only minimum cost per ending value preserves every potentially optimal continuation.
editorial: Keeping only minimum cost per ending value preserves every potentially optimal continuation.

tests.explanation: Replacing five with two makes the array strictly increasing in one operation.
No sequence of replacements can make arr1 strictly increasing.
